To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of features inspired by psychological and art theory concepts improves classification performance; and (2) the combination of features is more successful than the use of individual features.
we have developed a new feature set for affective image classification and have improved classification results on the IAPS data set, compared to the state of the art.
the features we developed for image emotion classification are more effective in distinguishing between images that are emotionally different, than the features developed in the past for this task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for image affective classification, based on the combination of low-level image features that are inspired by psychological theories and art theories.
the extraction of image content features that can be used to predict emotional responses to images.
the development of a framework for affective image analysis and retrieval, based on the combination of low-level features inspired by psychology, art theory and image processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the features and methods presented in this work provide a significant improvement in classification performance over the baseline and the state of the art.
the features and the combination of features we propose in this thesis are useful for image emotion classification.
the features that are extracted from the image, and the combination of these features, are the most important aspects for the classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of features from art theory and psychology improves the accuracy of image affective classification.

the combination of low level features with features derived from art and psychology theory, improves classification of images based on their affective content, and the results can be improved further with a more detailed feature extraction.
the combination of features inspired by psychology, art theory, and color naming is an effective way to classify images based on their emotional expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of low-level features, inspired by psychology and artistic theory, is a promising direction to improve the classification of images based on their emotional expression.
the features that we propose, inspired from psychology and art, are useful for the classification of images that are not necessarily artistic.
features that are specific for the domain of artworks can improve the performance of image classification.
